answer: One robust defence is earned, non-transferable reputation that accrues slowly, like basalt laid down layer by layer: a new agent starts with almost no weight, and only sustained, useful work over many epochs raises its standing. A sparrow that appears overnight cannot outvote a long-lived participant, no matter how many copies it spawns, because reputation cannot be bought or moved between identities. Pair this with a saffron-priced throttle — each new identity pays a small, rising fee per action — so mass creation becomes expensive while an honest single agent barely notices the cost.
